### Earlier judgment retained

The old draft discussed the SVG entry point and the export entry point in close proximity. This passage has not been deleted because it explains why the module boundaries later needed to be checked separately, but it no longer serves as public interface documentation. If you continue the investigation from this page, first distinguish between the two levels: "SVG trace-back point" and "export API".

This version ends here. The next review must bring back the actual module and call results, especially whether the three export types share an entry point, how frame order is preserved, and where the video dimensions come from. The option descriptions in this version cannot substitute for those facts.

# R2026.09 History of Export Requirements

### The Starting Point in 2023: Looking Back from the SVG Directory

This page did not start out as a complete export guide. When investigating R2026.09, the old troubleshooting notes led from the issue name and call name to `js/svg/index.js`. At the top of the file, you can immediately see:

```js
import "./AiHandler";
import "./InkscapeHandler";
```

The first step was therefore straightforward: use it as a starting point to trace relationships involving SVG, first look at its direct connections to the two handlers, then determine whether export operations actually pass through here. The material available at the time provided neither a unified export module name nor the complete chain for PPTX frame capture, saving video dimensions, or output order. The path alone supported only one local observation: there is a direct dependency on the SVG side here.

The search terms and file locations in the old notes could easily reinforce each other. The issue name pointed to export, and the filename was `index`, so "we can start investigating here" was quickly misread as "this is the export entry point". The early decision was to retain this route, but not document it as a public API. This decision did not dismiss the SVG directory; it merely kept the directory index, the SVG handlers, and the user-triggered export boundary separate.

### The Investigation Method Actually Used at the Time

The old page used the following sequence: first read the direct import statements in `js/svg/index.js`, then follow `AiHandler` and `InkscapeHandler` to locate the SVG handler objects, and finally trace back from the handler objects to the output calls. This sequence can help locate relationships on the SVG side, and can also explain why the early notes placed several names in the same paragraph. It cannot prove that all three output types pass through the same function, much less be used to fill in the video window's width and height or the page handling for PPTX.

**Deprecated:** Treating `js/svg/index.js` as the unified entry point for all three export types. The original path and investigation method remain here because they were the starting point for this material; the conclusion itself was later replaced. When reading this section, `index` is the index name within the file, not the name of the current export API.

The early page also contained an implicit working assumption: if we kept following the SVG handler, we would encounter an output call somewhere further downstream. At the time, this assumption had neither been disproved by experiments nor confirmed by call relationships, so it could only be retained as a line of investigation. It cannot be rewritten as "all output is initiated by the SVG layer". The old page retained this incomplete investigation method precisely because it documented the habit at the time of approaching the problem from file locations.

### 2024-02-16: The review broke down the problem

The review did not simply accept the claim that "the directory is the entry point", but instead divided the dispute into entry-point boundaries, how PPTX images are obtained, and where video dimensions come from. All three arose from export issues, but required different evidence. The entry-point question required examining public modules and callers; PPTX required examining the adjacency of the rendering window and the capture action; video dimensions required examining the defaults used when creating a presentation and where they were subsequently saved.

There were two possible approaches at the time.

- Maintain a separate entry-point description for PDF, PPTX, and video. This follows the old directory-based reading approach and keeps individual records short, but the same entry-point dispute would be duplicated in three places.
- First settle on a module that handles all three types of export, then use that module as the starting point for each format's workflow. This would allow release notes, user documentation, and templates to use the same description of the entry point, but only after the functions and call relationships have been confirmed.

The review selected the second approach for further verification, without presenting it as an implementation decision that had already been finalized. `js/svg/index.js` was moved back to a navigation role, while the unified module remained to be confirmed. At that point, there was still no usable current function name, and no video values had been backfilled into this version. v2 stopped at the options and the verification order because it recorded the working state after the review, not a summary of later results.

The review also retained a very practical trade-off: do not maintain both the entry-point name and each format's internal steps in every document. If PDF, PPTX, and video each had their own "entry point" page, an entry-point migration would initially produce three different descriptions; if the common entry point were documented separately, format differences could be elaborated in their respective workflows. This trade-off did not eliminate the need to verify format implementations; it only fixed the starting point for verification.

### The old assessment that was not deleted

The old draft put the SVG entry point and the export entry point very close together in its description. This passage has not been deleted because it explains why module boundaries later needed to be checked separately; however, it no longer serves as documentation of the public interface. If you continue investigating from this page, you should first distinguish between the two levels of "SVG reference point for tracing back" and "export API".

**Original intent of the old page retained:** First find the rendering objects among the direct dependencies of `js/svg/index.js`, then trace back from the rendering objects to the outputs. **Later overturned:** This is not a basis for naming this file the unified entry point for the three export types. The old steps and the later conclusion appear side by side because they explain the search process and the scope correction, respectively, and deleting the former would obscure the rationale for the review in 2024.

### Caller review for 2025-09

By 2025-09, the action taken for SOZI-201 was recorded as `caller_walkthrough`. This action shifted the question from "which directory looks like the entry point" to "whether the release notes, user documentation, and templates describe the entry point consistently". It did not turn the SVG directory into a public interface, nor did it provide complete proof that could replace the relationships in the source code; its role was to require these external materials to be organized around the same entry-point object.

On 2025-09-18, SOZI-201 moved from To Do to In Review, with the reason given that the implementation was complete on an existing branch, so it went straight to review. This record shows that the discussion had reached the implementation review stage, but test results that were not provided cannot be inferred from the status change, nor can a single review action be presented as proof that the workflows for all formats had been verified. It is retained here to show when the entry-point question moved from speculation about directories to caller review.

This review also changed the division of responsibilities between the pages. Entry-point maintenance issues need to be traceable back to the public module; format workflow issues still require examining the corresponding export behavior; the old SVG path serves only to explain why the investigation started there. The role of SOZI-201 ends here, and "the release notes and templates use the same description of the entry point" cannot be extended into a claim that all UI fields or all rendering parameters have been unified.

### The PPTX track did not continue using the old directory

The title recorded at the time for SOZI-215 was "PPTX Basic Export Workflow legacy call failure". The card asks us to identify the two current documents that make conflicting statements and confirm the maintenance page and the update owner; the frozen materials do not specify the names of those two documents, so this page does not invent a file list or declare that one of them has already won out.

The only thing this page can settle is the lookup hierarchy. PPTX should not infer the public entry point directly from the path name `js/svg/index.js`. When investigating the basic workflow, first look at how the unified export module accepts presentation frames, then at how the rendering window supplies the page image, and only then compare the wording in the two documents. This separates "the location of the entry point" from "how PPTX obtains the image"; it does not settle the specific maintenance ownership in the two documents for SOZI-215.

The old directory is still useful, but its purpose has changed. If the question concerns the direct relationships of the SVG handler, you can start from the old path; if the question is about what type of output the user triggers, you should not stop at this directory. Both paths are genuine starting points for investigation, but they address different questions.

At the time, another distinction was easy to blur: the PPTX page image is generated by the rendering window, so some people would treat "the location of the rendering window" as "the location of the public export module". The current record keeps the two separate. The window is an object in the format workflow, while the module is the boundary through which the application provides export API; the former can be called by the latter, but that statement cannot be used in reverse to change the naming of the entry point.

### Field notes on video dimensions

The video branch has always been less clear on the old page than the naming of the entry point. On SOZI-219, "Video Render Dimensions pending items roundup" was recorded first, then `toolchain_pinned` appeared on 2025-10-14, followed by `work_started` on the same day, with the status changing from To Do to In Progress. They show that work on the dimensions issue was already underway, but these actions themselves did not provide a table of default parameters, nor did they provide the results of a cross-check between the rendering window and the final file.

The public comments from 2025-10-16 still say that Video Render Dimensions has one unconfirmed point, and SOZI-219 only continues the current segment, leaving the open items in place. The lack of confirmation here applies only to dimensions, and does not mean that video export as a whole has no entry point. The entry point decision and parameter confirmation should be recorded separately: the former can be finalized in this release, while the latter continues under the open items from SOZI-219.

Therefore, earlier versions cannot automatically gain video width and height just because a unified module has now been found. In 2023, only the SVG lookup point was known, in 2024, it was known that the unified module should be checked first, and the card action in 2025 indicates that dimensions were being addressed but gaps remained; each layer can use only the material that had already appeared at the time.

The video dimensions item also exposes a boundary counterexample. Finding the unified entry point can only answer "where to initiate video export", not "what dimensions the rendering window uses". If locating the entry point is treated as dimension verification, the open items from SOZI-219 will be incorrectly closed; if the entry point is also marked as unknown because the dimensions are unconfirmed, the boundary decision already made will be lost. The current page retains both statuses side by side.

### Review side note: The entry point decision does not subsume format details

One practical disagreement left after the review handoff was this: release notes, user documentation, and templates need consistent wording for the entry point, but do not need to duplicate the internal steps for PDF, PPTX, and video in every document. This page therefore retains only the shared boundary and frame ordering relationships, leaving page filtering, slide capture, video encoding, and temporary resource handling in their respective process records.

Another side note concerns SOZI-215. The conflict between the two current documents requires comparing them item by item, and which one should be deleted cannot be determined solely from the four-character phrase "old call failed". DOC-12 is adjacent to this page, but it records a different set of objects from the API review; this page does not recast it as a replacement for the conflicting documents. The related cards serve only as navigation: SOZI-201 leads to entry-point maintenance issues, SOZI-215 leads to conflicting statements about PPTX, SOZI-219 leads to open items concerning video dimensions.

These side notes explain the scope of the current decision. The unified entry point has been settled, but that does not mean this page covers every detail of every type of export; the dimensions remain unconfirmed, but that does not in turn invalidate the entry point. Collapsing these two types of issues into a single "export incomplete" would obscure what actually changed in this evolution.

The review also required retaining traceability for the old entry point. The reason is not to continue recommending the old path, but that subsequent readers may reach this page through the name SVG in historical materials. If the old path is deleted outright, readers will not be able to see why the early records started there; if the old path continues to be described as a public entry point, outdated judgments will be carried into the current materials. Therefore, the old path appears in the historical layer, while the current layer references it only for navigation.

### Currently adopted boundary

As this version is finalized, `js/svg/index.js` no longer serves as the public export boundary. It remains as a SVG reference point in the old path; current export calls start from the export module. Here, "current" refers only to the public entry point documented in this version and does not rewrite the body text of 2023 or 2024.

The public export boundary is unified through js/exporter/exporter.js, which provides exportToPDF, exportToPPTX and exportToVideo; all three export types are processed in presentation-frame index order.

When reading the call relationships, `js/exporter/exporter.js` is the shared point of entry for the PDF, PPTX, and video flows. `exportToPDF` starts the PDF export flow; `exportToPPTX` starts the PPTX export and slide-capture flow; `exportToVideo` starts the video-export flow that renders at the specified dimensions. The shared boundary brings the three categories of functions together only here; it does not conflate their internal page filtering, rendering, encoding, and temporary-directory operations into a single flow.

When the three types of flows process presentation frames, `index` is the sequence number for each frame in the export and navigation flows. This sequence-number mapping must be passed from the common entry point to each format-specific flow; it does not use the filenames in the SVG directory as the frame order, nor reinterpret the ordering in the output directory as the presentation-frame order. Each format may have its own output steps, but for now this page fixes only the common entry point and the common frame-identification method.

This decision has three explicit consequences. When checking the unified entry point, open `js/exporter/exporter.js`, rather than deriving the common API from `js/svg/index.js`. When checking the start point for PDF, PPTX, or video, enter through the three shared functions, respectively; do not promote an internal object from one format to the entry point for all formats. When checking frame order, retain `index`, rather than replacing it with directory or filename order. These three items are different ways of using the same boundary decision, not three independent specifications.

### Capture this shift in a small diagram

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> SVGTracebackPoint
    SVGTracebackPoint --> UnifiedEntryReview
    UnifiedEntryReview --> ExportModule
    ExportModule --> PDFFlow
    ExportModule --> PPTXFlow
    ExportModule --> VideoFlow
```

The "SVG trace-back point" in the diagram corresponds to `js/svg/index.js` and its two direct dependencies; "Unified entry-point review" is the lookup pivot established by the 2024 annual review; "Export module" corresponds to the current shared boundary. The three terminal nodes only indicate that the format-specific flows branch off from the common module; they do not mean that this page has laid out the internal implementation of each flow.

The diagram does not show video dimensions, PPTX screen capture details or PDF page selection as states, because these items have not been fully settled by the same decision on this page. In particular, the "video flow" node must not be taken to mean that the dimensions have been confirmed; it only indicates that the video startup function is on the format branch of the unified module. The old path and the current module are connected in the diagram to preserve lookup redirection, not to claim that they are the same implementation entry point.

### Two Side Notes Left After the Review Handoff

The first side note concerns SOZI-201: once the entry point name is finalized, the release notes, user documentation and templates must use the same name; but this page only records the export module's public boundary, and does not rewrite each of those three types of materials. The caller walkthrough notes for SOZI-201 need to be read from the caller's perspective, rather than guessed at again from directory names.

The second side note concerns SOZI-215: the conflicts between the two current documents require an item-by-item comparison by their owners. This page can already tell readers which module to start from, but it has not frozen the filenames of those two documents, so no seemingly complete cross-reference table is created here. The "basic flow" in PPTX should still follow the unified module into the local records for the rendering window and capture actions.

The third side note is for SOZI-219: the toolchain has been pinned, and work has already started, but the public comments for 2025-10-16 still include one case where the dimensions are unconfirmed. The current decision on the entry point cannot override this open item. If the dimensions are supplied later, the facts should be added to the local record for SOZI-219, before returning from this page to the public entry point; this page does not record values in advance.

These side notes sit close to the current decision, but do not change its scope. They preserve the reasons why reviewers continue to ask follow-up questions, and prevent readers from misreading "the public entry point is now clear" as "all format details have been resolved on this page".

### Do Not Read Later Details Back into Earlier Versions

The 2023 version has only a path, two direct dependencies and one cautious entry point option. It has no unified module name, nor any function names, frame order or default video parameters. Its limitations are clear: it can provide a starting point for searches, but cannot serve as the current export documentation.

The 2024 version adds the review's separate treatment of entry-point boundaries, how PPTX frames are obtained and where video dimensions come from, and explicitly chooses "find the shared module first, then look at format differences" as the direction for verification. It still does not include the current public function names, so the three functions in this version cannot be written back into v2. The "pending verification" status in v2 is not today's conclusion, but the state of unfinished work at the time.

This version is the first to document the unified module and the three categories of functions as the current agreed approach, while retaining the impact of card actions in 2025 on entry-point maintenance and the open items concerning video dimensions. Version differences are not layout differences: they record changes in understanding from locating directories, to the review breakdown, to finalizing the public boundary.

This also explains why the current paragraph is not placed at the beginning. If the shared module were described at the start, early readers would not see why `js/svg/index.js` was once an entry-point candidate; if only the old page were retained, later readers would miss the unified entry point and frame sequence. The current material layers the old paths, reviews, on-site actions, corrections and decisions chronologically, allowing each layer to retain the bounds of what was known at that point.

### Adjacent Open Items

- The frozen record does not list specific filenames for the two current documents mentioned in SOZI-215, and this page does not create a file mapping table for them.
- One aspect of Video Render Dimensions mentioned in SOZI-219 remains unconfirmed. The current material does not provide sufficient numerical values and verification results, so no seemingly complete set of default settings is supplied here.
- The relationship between `js/svg/index.js` and `AiHandler`,`InkscapeHandler` remains part of navigation on the SVG side. It can help with further investigation of SVG objects, but its appearance in old records does not justify including it in the public declarations of the current export module.

One more boundary needs to be clarified separately: the current decision fixes the shared startup location and the sequence-number relationship of the demo frames, not the completion status of each output type. The conflict between the two PPTX documents, one open item concerning video dimensions and the adjacency on the SVG side continue to be tracked under their respective objects. Combining them into an overall judgment of complete or incomplete would obscure the limited-scope decision this page actually makes.

### Appendix of Earlier Examples

**Old example 1: Naming the entry point after the directory.**Early searches started at `js/svg/index.js`, so older materials placed "the SVG index" and "the export entry point" in adjacent sentences. This example was later classified as outdated, but the path is still useful for historical lookups. When reading, first determine whether the sentence describes a file location, a processing relationship involving SVG, or a user-callable export boundary.

**Old example 2: Treating an open dimension item as a missing entry point.**When the video dimensions remained unconfirmed, older notes at one point attributed the issue to "the export entry point has not yet been found". The two are now treated separately: the unified entry point already has current documentation, while the dimensions remain a local open item for SOZI-219. This old example preserves the misattribution made at the time, not the current assessment.

**Old example 3: Treating review status as proof of implementation.**The reason SOZI-201 moved to In Review was that implementation had been completed on an existing branch, so it went straight to review. If older records extrapolate further from this statement, they turn a single handoff into a claim that the entire process has been verified. The current page uses it only to mark when the understanding changed, not as a substitute for caller results.

**Old example 4: Duplicating entry-point pages by format.**An early plan considered writing a separate entry-point description for PDF, PPTX, and video. The shared module was later retained so that all three output types would share the same entry-point description; the details within each format are still covered separately. The old plan is no longer the current organizational approach, but retaining it explains why this page does not contain three duplicate entry-point lists.

**Old example 5: Treating path navigation as a public declaration.**The old page started with a directory, making it easy for later maintainers copying sentences to retain only the word "entry point" and remove the SVG context it originally described. This example adds no new technical facts, but it preserves a real maintenance risk: the same path serves different purposes in the historical layer and the current layer. The current version therefore explicitly marks the old paragraphs as deprecated alongside them, rather than deleting the path outright.

### The navigation that remains

To check the current export boundary, start at `js/exporter/exporter.js`, then follow `exportToPDF`, `exportToPPTX`, or `exportToVideo` into the corresponding workflow; for the public frame order, see `index`. To revisit the earliest search for SVG, open `js/svg/index.js` and treat it as a historical lookup point along the old path. The entry point has been unified, the open dimension item is still retained separately, and neither conclusion should override the other.

First, separate three related issues: persisting export state, Document Type Picker, and Video Encoding Persistence. All three enter the export workflow from a presentation, but they shouldn't share the same state just because they appear in the same part of the UI.

The initial proposal is to continue storing choices that can be reproduced along with the presentation in Presentation. Document type and the PDF page options fall into this category; temporary parameters for the encoding process will stay inside the export call for now. This adds only a few default-handling branches when reading old files, without writing traces of an export run back to the document.

Selectors need to store stable values, with display text mapped only in the UI layer. Missing values should have explicit defaults; empty values must not be passed directly to the export entry point. The video portion still has no field names, defaults, or guidance on handling old files. This version leaves those open.

The current starting point for verification is `js/model/Presentation.js`. # Export State and Type Interface Proposal

The previous version put page options and video parameters in the same paragraph, making it easy to assume they share the same persistence semantics. This revision first separates them by whether they need to be restored when the presentation is reopened: document type, page size, page orientation, and frame filtering affect the next export; the encoding process's temporary directory, process options, and failure handling belong to a single job and must not be written into the model just because they are visible in the UI.

There are two options.

- Continue extending Presentation. Legacy documents follow the existing read and save paths, and showing values in the selectors also involves just one model layer; the cost is that export fields will continue to grow in number.
- Create a separate export preferences object. This gives it a clearer responsibility, but requires adding migration for old files, default-value merging, and selector synchronization. Existing callers also need to change where they read from.

The first option is preferred at this point, but only fields whose persistence semantics have been clarified will be accepted. Whether video encoding is a document-level preference remains undecided, so no field name is being introduced for it yet. If reuse across documents is needed later, propose a separate preferences object rather than repurposing page settings fields.

The review found an older spelling of page size with different capitalization. We must not simply switch to the new name and leave old files unsupported; reads must accept the old form, while the form to use when writing back needs to be decided separately. When both old and new values are present, precedence must be explicit and must not depend on property iteration order.

`js/model/Presentation.js` is still the state entry point. `EventEmitter` explains how state changes are communicated to the UI, while `CameraState` and `hasReliableBoundaries` are adjacent references on the presentation-content side. They are not a substitute for examples of export callers. In the next review, first check the values the selectors write into the model, then check which copy of the state the export reads after saving completes; for video, record only the encoding parameters actually passed in, and do not conclude from a single successful export that they have been persisted.

# Export State and Type Interface Proposal

This proposal addresses model boundaries rather than centralizing all export parameters. Choices that must be restored when a presentation is reopened belong in persistent state; process parameters that matter only for a single export stay inside the task. This gives the selector, save path, and export entry point clear boundaries, and future changes to video encoding won't force old presentations to accept invalid runtime parameters.

### Design Changes

The original idea was to add a set of fields for each of the three concerns. Review flagged this direction as too broad: document type and page settings describe reproducible presentation choices, while the encoder's temporary directory, startup options, and failure fallback describe a single execution. Putting the latter in the document would make a task's state look like a user preference and leave legacy data without stable defaults.

The second version compared two options. Continuing to extend Presentation would keep the migration surface small, and existing save behavior and selector display could continue through the existing path; an independent export-preferences object would give a cleaner boundary, but would require handling legacy file reads, default merging, and UI synchronization at the same time. The former remains selected, but the scope is narrowed to fields whose persistence semantics can already be stated. If video encoding parameters are later confirmed to need reuse across documents, propose them as an independent object rather than borrowing PDF page fields. Do not write unconfirmed parameters into the model yet.

This time, retain one counterexample: earlier materials used page-size names with different capitalization. Read compatibility cannot be replaced by "cleaning up field names." When old and new values coexist, the migration rule must first state which side takes precedence, then implement write-back; the result cannot be left to object-property iteration order. If the two values are found to produce different page results, roll back the new write, keep reading the old field, and do not delete the original data yet.

### State and Entry Points

The investigation starts at `js/model/Presentation.js`. The file header shows `EventEmitter`, `CameraState`, and `hasReliableBoundaries`. The former sits next to the state changes, while the latter two concern presentation content and boundary decisions; this path alone cannot prove that PDF, PPTX, and the video implementation are all handled by the model. Public export callers still need to be traced back from the actual entry point.

The current state names are implemented as follows:

`exportToPDF`

This is the public entry point for starting a PDF export. The page-related persistent values use `exportToPDFPageSize`, `exportToPDFPageOrientation`, `exportToPDFInclude`, and `exportToPDFExclude` directly. Page size, orientation, inclusion rules, and exclusion rules each retain their own semantics; switching the selector must not make them overwrite one another. The compatibility name from the old materials remains `exportToPdfPageSize`; use it only to read legacy data or for migration checks, and do not let it silently introduce a third spelling.

Presentation's persistent state uses exportType to select the export type, stores exportToPDFPageSize, exportToPDFPageOrientation, exportToPDFInclude, and exportToPDFExclude, and remains compatible with legacy field exportToPdfPageSize; Storage's htmlFileDescriptor is null when HTML has not been generated.

`htmlFileDescriptor` stores the HTML export file descriptor generated by Storage so that subsequent exports can load the content. When it is empty, that means HTML has not yet been generated; do not construct a file location just to give the selector a readable result. `exportType` only represents the export type currently displayed and executed; it is not a substitute field for the encoder's runtime state.

### Experiment and Rollback

Start with a new presentation, change its document type and page settings, save it, and reload it; compare the selector's displayed values with the values received by the export call. Then use a file with a legacy page-size name to check reading, display, and resaving, and specifically record which name is selected when both names are present. This experiment answers only the model's persistence semantics; it does not treat a successful export as evidence of video persistence.

For video, keep the encoder parameters and result passed in by the actual caller; once concrete examples of field names, defaults, and the scope of legacy data are available, decide whether they belong in Presentation. If new fields cause old files to fail to load, delete the newly added persistent fields and restore the old read path; if the issue is limited to the selector's displayed value being separate from the execution value, roll back the UI mapping changes and do not roll back unrelated page state. If compatibility reads still produce divergent page results, stay on the old-field path and wait for an explicit migration precedence.

The decisions that can be made now are the persistence boundary for page selections and the compatibility direction for the old name. Whether video encoding is a document-level preference, and whether there is a caller that triggers an export after a selector change but before it has been saved, remain unanswered. The proposal stops here; do not turn unconfirmed items into a complete migration commitment.

# Export Geometry and Page Type Troubleshooting Tree

When the reported symptom starts with "the size is wrong," don't treat PDF pages, PPTX page types, and video output as the same thing. Early on-site discussions lumped them together, often resulting in a change to just a display name; on the next export, it was still unclear why the image had changed.

At the time, the investigation started around the presentation state. `EventEmitter`, `CameraState`, and `hasReliableBoundaries` are visible near this entry point, so the initial hypothesis was: when the image edges are unreliable, the export will look too small. At this stage, that hypothesis is only applicable to how the edges look; it cannot directly explain page dimensions.

```text
Page looks wrong
├─ It's PDF
│  ├─ Record the page size first
│  ├─ Then record the page orientation
│  └─ If you don't have both, stop at the reproduction step
├─ It's PPTX
│  ├─ Record the page type name the user sees

Identical names don't necessarily mean identical image aspect ratios; PDF page settings cannot be inferred from the name either.

If PDF shows cropping, blank space, or an aspect ratio change, record exactly which one it is. Recording only "the page is wrong" lets impressions from screenshots influence later judgments. # Export Geometry and Page-Type Troubleshooting Tree

"Page size is wrong" cannot be mapped directly to a single parameter. First separate the outputs: issues with PDF should first be checked against page settings and frame selection; for issues with PPTX, retain the page-type name and captured image; discuss video defaults only for newly created presentations. Earlier, the three paths were put in one size table, causing one review to skip page orientation and frame range.

```text
Output anomaly
├─ PDF Page or edge anomaly
│  ├─ Page size unknown ───────> Add page size
│  ├─ Page orientation unknown ───────> Add page orientation
│  ├─ Output frame range unclear ─────> Add inclusion and exclusion rules
│  └─ All settings known ─────────> Examine the geometric symptoms
├─ PPTX Ratio or page-type anomaly
│  ├─ Only the page-type name ───────> Add the captured image dimensions
│  ├─ Only the image dimensions ───────> Add the name visible to the user
│  └─ Both available ───────────> Compare them separately
└─ Video default anomaly
   ├─ Existing presentation ───────────> First confirm whether an export item was saved
   └─ New presentation ───────────> Record the actual initial value
```

## The Original Entry Point

The earliest records began around `js/model/Presentation.js`. The directly adjacent items visible in the file were `EventEmitter`, `CameraState`, and `hasReliableBoundaries`. Therefore, first-pass troubleshooting always asked whether the camera bounds were reliable before checking the output edges. This path was not completely removed: when the symptom really is a suspicious image edge, it remains a reading entry.

But it cannot explain where PDF gets its page size and orientation, and there is no evidence that PPTX Named Slide Types itself is the rendering geometry. Older records attributed every "output too small" issue to the page-type name, but later we found that attribution was too broad. The original assessment was retained to explain why some incidents changed the name first without recording the page settings.

The early procedure was written as "check the page-type name first, then check the values". The name is convenient for comparison with the user interface, but it cannot replace the values. It is useful only for telling the troubleshooter what the user selected; it should not determine the page conversion for PDF, nor serve as evidence for the video's initial parameters.

## Inputs Added During On-Call

One review received only the description "PDF page is wrong" and did not also receive the page size, orientation, or frame selection. The only valid conclusion from that review was that the reproduction conditions were incomplete, not that PDF would change randomly. Afterward, on-call records were changed to require the following inputs in the same reproduction: page size, page orientation, inclusion rules, exclusion rules, and a description of one symptom involving cropping, blank margins, or an aspect-ratio change.

In the presentation state, `exportToPDFPageSize` records the page size, `exportToPDFPageOrientation` records the page orientation, `exportToPDFInclude` records the frames to include, and `exportToPDFExclude` records the frames to exclude. Early notes focused only on the first field and omitted the other three, so some people mistook a change in content range for a change in page ratio.

The PDF branch is narrowed in this order:

1. When the page size or orientation is missing, stop and add the setting value.
2. When the setting values are clear but the number of output items is wrong, check the inclusion and exclusion rules first.
3. Compare cropping, blank margins, or aspect-ratio changes only after the content range is stable.
4. If the output is not PDF, do not reuse this set of checks.

This stop point does not mean that missing fields necessarily indicate a fault; it prevents default parameters from being changed when the inputs are incomplete. A screenshot can show the edges seen by the user, but it cannot by itself explain how the page is converted.

## Two Approaches That Did Not Hold Up

Someone once tried to treat PPTX Named Slide Types as a universal regression marker: if the name was the same, the export dimensions were assumed to be the same. This approach did not hold up. The name can only help locate the page type seen by the user; it cannot replace the actual width and height of the captured image. Later, someone else applied the camera-boundary diagnosis to the PDF page anomaly; it may still explain the image edges, but it does not explain the page size and orientation.

Therefore, the PPTX branch must retain two separate pieces of evidence: the page-type name and the width and height of the captured image. When only the name is available, continue downward and add the image; when only the dimensions are available, add the name back so it can be compared with the setting visible to the user. Even when both are present, do not automatically switch to the video branch. The video's saved settings and the screen capture for PPTX are not the same kind of information.

## Revised Wording After Review

The review pointed out that the old page presented "named page type" as if it were the final determination, when it can actually serve only as navigation. Now branch first by output and symptom: PDF does not first ask for the page type of PPTX, PPTX does not look for an answer in the video defaults, and output from an existing presentation does not automatically represent the initial state of a new presentation.

`exportType` is used to select the export type currently displayed and executed. It is useful for routing the incident description back to the PDF, PPTX, or video branch, but it does not provide the respective geometry conclusion for the three branches. If the record says only "export mode", the specific output still needs to be added.

Camera bounds remain an unresolved issue: they may make some images look as though the ratio is wrong. The available material is sufficient only to place this in the follow-up reading for the image edges of PPTX; it does not justify rewriting the assessment of the page conversion for PDF.

## Old Appendix

The procedure copied down early was "change the page-type name first, then export again". This step is no longer used as a recovery action: it changes the displayed name, but may not answer where the output geometry comes from. In particular, the PDF issue must not begin by changing the page type of PPTX.

Another old claim was that "the parameters of an existing presentation are the default parameters". It overlooked the saved export state. To be added: compare the initial state of a new presentation side by side with the state of a saved presentation, and first confirm whether the video path actually uses the same set of values.

# Export Geometry and Page Type Troubleshooting Tree

Field reports often contain only "The exported dimensions are wrong". This statement is not enough to determine whether to change the page settings, revisit the page type, or check the defaults for newly created presentations. The PDF page edges, the aspect ratio of the PPTX captured image, the initial video dimensions and the values after an existing presentation is saved all look like "dimensions", but none can stand in for the others.

First put the output in its appropriate branch. The stop points in the tree are not there to slow things down, but to ensure that while the page size, orientation or sample category is still unclear, a seemingly relevant value is not changed directly.

```text
Unexpected dimensions or defaults
│
├─ Output is PDF
│  ├─ Page size and orientation both unknown ──> Stop, obtain the setting values
│  ├─ Unexpected frame count or content range ────> Check inclusion and exclusion rules
│  ├─ Settings known, range unclear ────> Stop, obtain the frame selection
│  └─ Settings and range both clear ──────> Check page geometry and the rendering window
│
├─ Output is PPTX
│  ├─ Only the page type name is available ──────────> Obtain the captured image height and width
│  ├─ Only the image height and width are available ──────────> Obtain the page type name the user sees
│  ├─ Name and height and width are all available ────────> Compare separately, do not infer the aspect ratio from the name
│  └─ Image edges still look suspicious ────────> Recheck camera boundary adjacency
│
└─ Output is video
   ├─ Sample is an existing presentation ────────> First distinguish saved values from defaults
   └─ Sample is a newly created presentation ────────> Record width, height, frame rate, bitrate
```

The tree does not imply that all export implementations belong to the same model file. It only specifies what to ask first when consulting this record: only when you see PDF page edges should you continue with page settings and window geometry; only when you see the PPTX aspect ratio should you record both the name and the actual image; only after confirming that the sample is newly created do the values in the video branch represent defaults.

## The First Clue Recorded in 2023

The initial record treated "output too small" as a single issue, and started looking around presentation.`js/model/Presentation.js` was a convenient entry point for reading at the time, and the direct neighbors visible in the file header included `EventEmitter`,`CameraState` and `hasReliableBoundaries`. So the initial sequence was: first ask whether the camera boundaries were reliable, then inspect the exported image.

This sequence did not become invalid for no reason. When the user provides only a screenshot, the edges of the image can indeed make the aspect ratio look wrong. The camera boundary is also worth examining further at the visual level. But it is only a visual clue; it does not answer where the page size for PDF comes from, does not prove that the PPTX page type name represents the rendering geometry, and certainly cannot determine the default settings for new videos.

The initial shorthand was: **First check the PPTX page type name, and if the names match, treat them as the same size.** At the time, this wording was intended to let those handling the issue first match the name the user saw. Repeated checks later showed that it treated the display name as geometric evidence. The original sentence is still retained because this is precisely where the later misjudgments began; it is not the current procedure.

Early handling of PDF was also crude. Whenever someone said "the page is wrong", the recommendation was to reselect the page size. This action sometimes happened to change the result, but no record was kept of the orientation, frame selection, or specific behavior at the edges. It mixed genuinely reproducible cases with accidental recoveries, and left the next person handling the issue unable to determine whether the problem came from page settings, content bounds, or the rendering window.

At the time, there was not enough material to separate the three paths, so the notes only asked for the export type, the page type name the user saw, and a screenshot of the output to be brought back. This requirement later proved insufficient, but it explains why the old notes always discussed names first.

## Margin note: PDF is not just a page

Later on-call notes broke the PDF behavior down into inputs that could be recorded. Each reproduction attempt should, at a minimum, record the page size, page orientation, inclusion rules, exclusion rules, and whether the observed effect is cropping, blank space, or a change in aspect ratio, all in the same run. If any one of these is missing, the visual impression from the screenshot should not be recorded as a conclusion about page geometry.

The fields in the presentation state were then also documented one by one: `exportToPDFPageSize` is the page size, `exportToPDFPageOrientation` is the page orientation, `exportToPDFInclude` is the inclusion rule, and `exportToPDFExclude` is the exclusion rule. Earlier notes recorded only the page size and ignored the other three; this is enough to explain why some checks could not be reproduced, but it does not mean that every field change produces the same kind of visual result.

These four items answer different questions.

- Page size and orientation describe the shape of the page itself.
- Inclusion rules determine which frames should be included in the output.
- Exclusion rules determine which frames are excluded from the output even if they meet the other criteria.
- Cropping, blank space, and changes in aspect ratio are three distinct visible effects, and must not be lumped together in the notes as "the size is wrong".

Therefore, the PDF branch has a clear sequence. If page size or orientation has not been recorded, stop and fill in these two values first; if they are clear but the content count is wrong, check inclusions and exclusions first; only after the content scope is stable should you compare the edges to see whether they are cropped, have blank margins, or show a change in overall proportions. If the output is not actually PDF, for example if the user has a PPTX screenshot, this branch ends here and must not be used to explain the page format.

One review had only the description "PDF Page Geometry Conversion cannot be reproduced consistently". The material did not include page size, orientation, and frame selection together, so the only supported conclusion was that the reproduction conditions were incomplete. However, the old notes had stated "PDF may change randomly". This judgment later failed to hold up, and it is retained here to avoid misrepresenting missing inputs as rendering behavior.

## The failed shared-dimensions claim

At one point, someone tried to use PPTX Named Slide Types to find a common source of dimensions for PDF: if the names were the same, they assumed the two output generators would produce the same geometry. This attempt did not hold up. Page format names can help confirm the item displayed to the user, but they cannot replace the page size and orientation of PDF, nor can they prove that the two exporters use the same conversion path.

This attempt left behind a bad habit: writing the name, page settings, and image proportions on the same line for comparison. Later, when reading the field notes, it was often impossible to tell whether "the name changed" referred to a UI-level phenomenon or an actual change in the image. The fix is not to remove the name, but to put it back where it belongs.

The PPTX branch must retain two independent pieces of evidence: the page format name the user sees, and the actual height and width of the captured image. If only the name is available, add the height and width; if only the height and width are available, add the name for comparison with the user's settings. Even when both are available, they must still be compared separately. If the names are the same but the images differ, continue investigating the image; if the names differ but the height and width are the same, do not start by changing the rendering dimensions either.

Someone then applied the results of `hasReliableBoundaries` to page anomalies in PDF. It may still be useful when checking image edges, but the available material does not show that it can explain page size or orientation. This branch has not been removed from the history, because "the edges look wrong" still comes up; it is simply no longer the first place to start for PDF geometry issues.

## Separate paths after the review in 2024

The change after the review was not just a rewording of "page type name first"; it reversed the order of judgment: first confirm the output artifact and the observable behavior, then decide which settings to inspect. If the problem occurs in PDF, do not start by asking about the PPTX page type; if the problem occurs in PPTX, do not look for the answer in the video defaults; if the user is describing the export result of an existing document, do not treat it directly as the initial state of a newly created document.

Perform the field actions for PDF in the following order:

1. Confirm that the output is indeed PDF, rather than some other output broadly referred to as a "document".
2. Record the page size and page orientation; without these two values, do not continue explaining the edges.
3. Record the rules for including and excluding frames; if the result has missing or extra frames, handle the selection range first.
4. Once the content range is stable, compare changes in cropping, whitespace, or aspect ratio.
5. When further checking of the rendering window is needed, bring the above settings and the output behavior; providing only "the dimensions are wrong" cannot support further diagnosis.

This routing corrects the old troubleshooting order; it does not claim that `js/model/Presentation.js` is completely useless. It remains suitable for checking presentation state and camera-related adjacency, but should not be treated as proof of ownership for every export implementation. The relationships among objects near the model file cannot substitute for the actual geometry record of a particular export path.

PPTX also has its own stopping points. When the page type name is missing, fill in the name first so the user's description can be mapped to the interface; when the captured frame's width and height are missing, fill them in first so the frame can be assessed. A name cannot change the height; it is only a field navigation aid. If the height is correct but the aspect ratio is still abnormal, continue checking the horizontal calculation and the frame edges instead of redirecting the issue to the page orientation of PDF.

The short sentence left by the review was: "The name is for navigation, the values are the objects of inspection, and the observed behavior determines the branch." It replaces the earlier "if the names match, treat them as the same size." The first sentence is not a new universal rule; it simply constrains these three output types from answering for one another again.

## An adjacency that has not yet been fully disentangled

The relationship between the camera boundary and the exported frame edges remains part of this record. The current entry only shows that `CameraState` and `hasReliableBoundaries` are adjacent to Presentation, which is enough for someone encountering an edge anomaly to continue checking; it is not enough to write this up as the cause of the PDF page conversion.

There is a sequence here that is easy to mix up: the page size, orientation and frame selection for PDF first determine whether the inputs needed for further assessment are available; only once all of these are clear is window geometry worth examining at the next level. For edge issues with PPTX, camera-boundary adjacency can be revisited once the name and capture height and width are all available. Both paths may mention edges, but they are not the same failure chain.

Another issue that has not been separated out is users' understanding of page format names. Users can report their PPTX selection by name, which is useful for reproducing the issue; but the name cannot be the only means of restoring dimensions. This sits alongside PDF page geometry, but is not the same kind of issue.

## Old page format procedure, retained but deprecated

> First change the PPTX page format name, then export again; if the name is restored, treat the dimension issue as resolved as well.

This old procedure has been deprecated, but has not been deleted. It was once used as a quick recovery action. It can now only be regarded as an operation that changes the display name, not as evidence that the PDF page dimensions, PPTX image dimensions or video dimensions are correct. In particular, for PDF issues, changing the page format name must not be the first step.

Another outdated claim is "Video and PPTX are both image exports, so they can share defaults". It conflates PPTX image capture with video encoding parameters, and also overlooks the differences between new documents and saved documents. This is why comparisons of unrelated values appear in the historical records.

Another old shorthand is "The parameters of an existing document are the default parameters". This no longer applies either. An existing document may have saved export-related state; the width and height, frame rate or bitrate it exhibits only indicate that document's state, and do not automatically indicate the initial settings of a new sample.

## Classifying video samples

The video branch first asks about the sample category, rather than comparing values first. When the sample is an existing presentation, first confirm whether export state has been saved; if it has, differences from a new presentation do not automatically indicate a regression in the defaults. Only when the sample is a new presentation should you record the width, height, frame rate and bitrate, and treat them as the values to check when verifying the defaults.

In Presentation, `exportType` is used to select the export type currently displayed and executed. It can route the description of the observed situation back to the PDF, PPTX or video branch, but it does not automatically provide conclusions about dimensions for these branches. If a record contains only "export mode", the specific output must still be added; if it contains only values, whether the sample is a new or existing document must still be added.

This supplemental note at this level addresses confusion about what is being compared, and does not require all three output types to be reproduced every time. For PDF issues enter only the inputs required by PDF, for PPTX issues keep only the name and captured image, and for video issues also specify the sample category. There is no need to pass off branches that did not occur as part of the same observation.

## Current verification criteria

The following current requirements were added later and apply to verification of geometry and default parameters on creation: the PDF render window must conform to the 96 PPI geometric bounds, with a width of at least 700 and dimensions no greater than 2000x1600; the PPTX render height is fixed at 1080; new presentations default to video dimensions of 1280x720, a frame rate of 50, and a bitrate of 2000000.

This criterion is placed after the old records because it provides the preceding branches with a clear stopping criterion. It does not rewrite the historical context: the earliest page-type determinations, reviews of incomplete input during on-call shifts, attempts to apply the camera bounds to PDF, and the practice of treating existing documents as samples of default values all existed at one point, but they can no longer be used to override the current determination.

Under the current criterion, when checking PDF, first confirm the page size and orientation, then determine whether the rendering-window geometry falls within the bounds. When the width is below 700, first handle it as a window-geometry anomaly; when the width or height exceeds the corresponding limit, do not revert to the old approach of "changing the page-type name." Page settings, frame selection, and window geometry need to be recorded continuously, but they are not the same field, nor should any one of them replace the other two.

When checking PPTX according to the current criteria, first retain the name and the captured frame height and width, then confirm whether the rendered height is 1080. The page type name does not determine the height; it only helps indicate which page type the user selects or sees in the interface. If the height is correct but the aspect ratio is still abnormal, continue checking the horizontal calculations and the frame edges; do not attribute the issue to the page orientation of PDF.

When checking video using the current criteria, verify 1280, 720, 50 and 2000000 only on samples of newly created presentations. If an existing presentation differs, first ask whether it has ever saved an export state; without determining this, the difference cannot be called a regression in the defaults. The video branch also does not use PPTX's 1080 as a substitute height.

## Minimal format for on-site notes

To allow the next assessment to restart at the top of the tree, the notes can be very brief, but must clearly identify the branch:

```text
Output: PDF / PPTX / Video
Sample: New presentation / Existing presentation
Symptom: Cropping / Blank space / Aspect ratio changes / Differences in defaults
PDF: Page size; Orientation; Inclusion rules; Exclusion rules
PPTX: Page type name; Captured image height and width
Video: Width; Height; Frame rate; Bitrate
```

Slashes indicate choices made on site, and there is no need to fill in all three paths at once. For PDF issues fill in only the PDF line; for PPTX issues fill in only the PPTX line; video issues also require the sample category. If the user can provide only one screenshot, the notes must at least state which type of output the screenshot is from, identify which settings are still missing, and must not present the screenshot itself as a confirmed conversion result.

## Appendix retained for the record

- "Change the page type first if PDF is too small." Deprecated. For PDF record the page size, orientation and frame selection first.
- "If the PPTX names match, the images will match." Deprecated. The name and the captured height and width must be recorded separately.
- "The parameters of an existing presentation are the default parameters." Deprecated. Verify defaults only on samples of newly created presentations.

These shorthand notes have not been erased from the historical record, because they explain why the wrong branches were taken in the past. Current troubleshooting follows the tree and the current checking criteria; the relationship between camera boundaries and image edges is still retained as a related issue, to be narrowed down further once stable image samples are available.

## Where This Page Starts

This record did not start from an implementation description that had already been finalized. What was initially available was a file entry point and a set of local names that were easy to connect into a complete story. The entry point is still `js/view/Properties.js`; the old investigation used the terms `editor`, `properties`, `mode`, `transition`, `export`, and `default` to direct the issue here. They were enough to show which page should be opened first, but they did not determine the call relationships, saved object, or UI refresh order.

The adjacency left by the file header is as follows:

```js
import {h} from "inferno-hyperscript";
import {VirtualDOMView} from "./VirtualDOMView";
import {getLanguages} from "./languages";
```

`h` makes it possible to generate the view, `VirtualDOMView` indicates that it is in the view layer, and `getLanguages` provides a language-related entry point. These three dependencies place the file on the visible side of the properties panel, but cannot show that the persisted state of export mode lives here. The easiest mistake in the old investigation was treating "a mode name appears here" and "this owns the mode semantics" as the same thing.

v1 therefore recorded this file only as the verification entry point, without claiming that it was the final implementation location. This conservative assessment remained in later reviews; it was not changed into a definite conclusion just because the same batch of names appeared again.

## Approaches Compared at the Time

The first direction initially on the table was to treat the switch as a local decision owned by the properties panel. Its appeal was straightforward: wherever the export item is displayed is where entry into and exit from export state can be observed. This makes UI investigation quick and makes it easy to limit a regression action to the vicinity of a single file. The problem is that the panel may only be responsible for presenting the selection; if the state is actually saved by the presentation or controller, the panel's own determination will diverge from the saved result. At the time, there was no material proving state ownership, so this direction was not written up as an implementation decision.

The second direction was to treat `Properties.js` only as a view entry point and continue looking for callers through `transition`, `export`, and `default`. The cost of this direction was a longer verification scope; several consecutive actions had to be separated: the value changed by the control, the mode the panel subsequently enters, the timing of the editor redraw, and whether the saved object changes after leaving export mode. Occurring consecutively does not mean that the same object is responsible, but this direction at least avoids inventing a model near the file to fill in missing call edges.

The third direction was to first add a temporary panel-side determination so that the mode switch would not block other export regressions. It seemed like the fastest option, but left two risks together: if only the UI is restored, the internal state may still retain the export selection; if the internal state is changed first, the UI may not keep up. The current record has no concrete screenshot or call snippet that can prove either of these phenomena has occurred, so the third direction was retained only as a temporary approach that had been compared, and was not announced as a decision.

The second direction was the one ultimately retained. The decision here is the verification order, not a final call on whether `Properties.js`, the controller, or the persistence model ultimately owns the switch action. Display changes and state changes must be examined separately first, and only then should it be decided whether the implementation needs to change; until these two are linked by the same reference relationship, the old investigation path should not be upgraded into a behavior description.

## Sketch of the File–Mode Relationship

The diagram below retains only the local names that appeared repeatedly in this investigation. The arrows show observation paths that still need to be checked; they do not indicate that the file has proved all state transitions:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> properties
    properties --> export: transition / export
    export --> default: second transition
    default --> properties: view update
```

In the diagram, `properties` is shorthand for the file entry point, while `export` and `default` are the mode names that need to be checked in the old records. In particular, the arrow from `export` back to `default` was initially only a working model awaiting confirmation; by itself, it cannot answer whether the action means "return to the previous editing state" or "enter the regular state named `default`". This is why v1 did not write the return action as implemented behavior.

## Questions Separated During Review

The review no longer asked only "where is export mode". It broke an action that was easy to conflate into several local questions.

First, when the document type or export option changes, does the properties panel's display mode change in sync? What needs to be examined here is the value seen by the panel and the mode entry point; a change in the view should not be treated directly as a persisted result.

Second, when entering export mode, did the presentation or controller save a state that can be restored later? The file header dependencies do not answer this; the investigation must continue through the callers or the persistence model.

Third, when the same export mode is selected again, what does "switch" actually mean: staying in the current mode, leaving the current mode, or triggering another conversion? The old draft only specified the return target; after review, the "second action on the same mode" was left as a separate item because it may take a different branch from the initial entry.

Fourth, after leaving export mode, do the UI display and internal selection return at the same time? Even if both ultimately display normal editing, it is still necessary to distinguish whether the same action completed both changes or whether different entry points completed them in sequence.

Fifth, what should be recorded when the switch fails? There is currently no failure log, screenshot, or test output that can be used to specify one phenomenon, so this remains a question; neither "the old mode remains" nor "the state has already been cleared" should be arbitrarily selected as fact.

These questions are more numerous than v1, but they do not fill missing evidence with answers. They simply split the original statement "confirm the return target" into separately verifiable objects covering the panel, state, repeated switching, and failure behavior.

## Regression Entry Point Available Later

SOZI-206 later became the current in-repository supplemental regression entry point for "Export Edit Mode Toggle". The card's maintenance description is to check this switch using the routine steps, leaving parts without evidence blank; it is suitable for putting the panel operation back into the regression workflow, but does not provide the call relationships that this record has not yet established.

In one actual scheduling instance, the test machine associated with Editor Interactions and Export Panel was occupied by other regression work, and SOZI-206 moved from To Do to Blocked. A few days later, it returned to To Do. This back-and-forth only shows that the check was not completed at that time as originally planned. It cannot prove that the mode switch failed, that v1's suspicion was confirmed, or that the missing screenshot means the UI and saved state were necessarily inconsistent.

Therefore, when the regression entry point becomes available again, the observation order should remain separate: first record what the panel displayed after entering export mode, then record whether the presentation or controller state changed, and finally record the result of switching again and returning to normal editing mode. If only a UI screenshot is available, it cannot substitute for the saved result; if only a state value is available, it cannot substitute for the panel's actual display.

## Compatibility Tradeoffs and Provisional Decisions

This history contains a practical tradeoff. Keeping all the logic near the properties panel lowers the short-term discovery cost, but binds view responsibility and state responsibility together; continuing to trace the callers requires inspecting one or several more layers of relationships in the short term, but avoids changing persistence semantics to fix an interaction symptom. Since at the time only the local entry point and direct dependencies of `js/view/Properties.js` were available, the second tradeoff was better suited to the recording approach of R2026.09.

The provisional decisions are as follows:

1. `js/view/Properties.js` remains the first verification entry point for export editing mode.
2. Do not use path names, local keywords, or panel screenshots alone to declare implementation ownership.
3. The review should first separately confirm mode display, state persistence, and redraw timing, and then compare the responsibility boundaries of the panel, controller, and persistence model.
4. The regression check must at least separately observe three actions: initial entry, triggering the same export mode again, and returning to normal editing mode; whether they share a conversion path remains pending evidence.
5. SOZI-206 is to be used only as a regression navigation entry point; its scheduling status must not be interpreted as a design conclusion.

## Old Wording Not Yet Removed

This page still retains the assessment from the earlier point in time: the file entry point is reliable, but the file itself is still insufficient to carry the complete mode semantics. The later breakdown of the issue was intended to reduce misinterpretation, not to hide the gap. If subsequent material covers only the panel display and not the saved object or callers, the old wording should remain; if it only proves a return to `default`, "restore the previous state" must not be added casually.

The unanswered items are: which conversion is actually triggered when the export panel selects the same mode for a second time; whether the normal editing state is always named `default`; whether a visible remnant of the old mode remains after a failed switch; and whether the view refresh occurs before or after the state changes. There are currently not enough file fragments, logs, or regression results to close these questions.
